utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-98-30/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Kvocka, Milojica Kos, Zoran Zigic, Mladjo Radic, and Dragoljub Prcac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the late start, but because of the late finish of the previous trial in this courtroom and the need to run the tapes for half an hour after it is finished because of the delayed transmission caused the delay. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. This is the first that has been called since the judgement, and of course we are not in any real position to know what is happening. Nevertheless, there may be some questions which will arise. For the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Norman Farrell for the Prosecution, with Mr. Anthony Carmona, and Mr. Wolfgang Sakulin is the case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dr. Zoran Jovanovic from Belgrade, and I shall today be representing the accused Mladjo Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Prcac. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Jovan Simic, lawyer here for the accused Prcac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Kos.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Zarko Nikolic with Mr. Matt Hennessey. We are here for the accused Milojica Kos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And for Mr. Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Slobodan Stojanovic, lead counsel for Mr. Zigic. And I'd like to seize this opportunity to raise a -- to mention a technical problem. I cannot hear the interpretation. I'm afraid my headphones are not in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand? There's no need to stand up. THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. We have received a message from your counsel that he is unwell and the doctor has advised him not to attend, but he says that he has no issues to raise at this hearing. We did suggest to him that if he wished to consult other counsel in the case he should, but in any event, he will be able to raise anything later on an informal basis if anything does arise. Do you understand that? THE ACCUSED KVOCKA: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The accused is nodding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Mr. Radic, are you able to understand the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphones of the accused are not on, and we cannot hear what they are saying. THE ACCUSED RADIC: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I can hear. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Prcac, are you able to hear the proceedings? THE ACCUSED PRCAC: [Interpretation] Yes, I am very well. I can hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kos. THE ACCUSED KOS: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And Mr. Zigic? THE ACCUSED ZIGIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Yes, I can hear you, and I can hear the interpretation in the language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The present stage of this appeal is that the appellants have been granted an extension of time, until the 15th of April, in which to file their appellant's briefs. I would like to draw the attention of counsel to the terms of the current Rule 108. Although you were not bound by that at the time you filed your notices of appeal, the Rules by which you are bound in relation to your appellant's brief requires you to set out in the appellant's brief your grounds of appeal. Now, the new Rule 108 defines what a ground of appeal is, and it seems to be that it was necessary to insert this definition because of some inability of some counsel to understand. What you have to do is to identify the order, decision or ruling which you challenge, with a specific reference to the date of its filing and/or the transcript page, and you are required to indicate the substance of the alleged errors and the relief sought. That sounds very simple. Unfortunately, a lot of counsel do not understand it. But there must be a clearly identified set of grounds of appeal in your appellant's brief so that we know what this appeal is about. It's no good just having a discursive discussion of the case with, every now and again, a complaint about something. We want a numbered series of propositions asserting grounds of appeal with the arguments attached to them. So please do remember that when you are finalising your grounds of appeal. Mr. Stojanovic, I would like to make it very clear to you at the outset that the Appeals Chamber will not accept the torrent of paper that you inflicted upon the Trial Chamber. If you are going to constantly bring motions which do not succeed, you will find, as you found the other day, that you will be denied your costs of them. So let's start off on the proper basis. We only want to hear from you in motions if you have something really important to deal with, merely because you may fail if a motion will not deny you your costs, but if we regard the motion as frivolous, you will. Now, there have been three that you've made so far. Each of them has been unsuccessful. One of them you've lost your costs; another one, I have to say I can only assume that the President did not have that particular provision drawn to his attention. So in future, just be careful before you start sending us some motions. Now, is there anything that the Prosecution wants to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Is there anything that any counsel wants to raise within the terms of Rule 65 bis about the proceedings or in relation to the condition of their client's health and incarceration? Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. If I may, I'm not trying to excuse myself, it is merely that I interpreted differently the decision of the Trial Chamber, with which I go along. I merely wanted the Prosecution to go by it. I was not against any of the acts adopted. I merely wanted the other party to apply that consistently. So whatever I did, I didn't do it of a whim, because of a whim. What I nevertheless wish to say is that in a certain manner, this may lead to another motion, and that is the expansion of the number of pages of the appeal, because there are so many problems with the first-instance judgement, which we tried to resolve in part before the appeal, before we laid the ground for our appeal. However, obviously we shall have to resolve it in the very text of the reasoning for the appeal, and therefore our appeal will be longer. This Defence has, too, objections to the text of the first-instance judgement, and that is the reason why we wanted to alleviate the burden of the Appellate Chamber before we filed the appeal by filing some preliminary motions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you better make any application - this applies to all counsel - you better make any application for an extension of the number of pages well in advance, because usually we find we get these motions on the last day or so, which means we either allow it simply out of frustration or we order you to go away and redo your briefs in a shorter form. So if you, in the course of your preparations, you are seeing that you are obviously going to exceed the limits imposed by the practice direction, I suggest you make your application well and truly in advance. I myself take the view that the principal purpose of the practice direction was to cure the extravagance of both parties, which included the Prosecution, in the size of the briefs which they used to file, sometimes six or seven hundred pages long, mainly quoting large slabs of evidence or authorities. That was its purpose. The consequences of the practice direction I think probably caused more trouble than it's worth, but nevertheless, it is being enforced. But so far as I'm concerned, as the Pre-Appeal Judge, I will grant extensions very readily, provided, as I say, we get a fair estimate of what it will take and provided that it does not seem grossly excessive in the way in which we used to have to put up with in relation to briefs. Now, the 15th of April may seem a long way away, but it's only about five weeks. So I suggest that you should get on to your applications within the next couple of weeks. You must be able to see by now approximately how many pages you need. And I also take the view that if the -- if one party gets an extension, the other party will automatically get one as well. From the Prosecution's point of view, of course, they will want to file, I suppose, a joint response, respondent's brief, and we will listen in the same way to them as we listen to the appellants' counsel for an extension of pages. From what I have seen of this decision, there is certainly a number of controversial issues in it which one or other party is going to have to spend a lot of time explaining. So don't worry too much. You will get your extensions and, I repeat, provided that you make your applications early enough. Now, is there anything that any other counsel for the appellants wishes to raise? Very well, then. Well, in relation to Mr. Kvocka, if his counsel wishes to raise any matter, having seen the transcript or having discussed the matter with his colleagues, he may do so informally with the Senior Legal Officer of the Appeals Chamber, and we will deal with it as far as possible on an informal basis. Thank you for your attendance. I will now adjourn.
